#+title: Selected-input test replay capsules

* Scope
artifact.replay constructs a bounded DATA capsule and a deterministic test
admission plan. It never starts tests, Nix, tools, services or realms. Main must
bind live runtime/test admission and run through the existing test/native
execution path. A capsule contains no execution grant, borrowed handle, process
identity, environment snapshot, credentials or mutable application/database state.

This is selected-file replay input capture, not complete failure replay. Tests
may depend on undeclared files, network services, mutable data, time, randomness
or process interleavings. Those dependencies are not reconstructed by this
module. Supporting files must be listed explicitly; test outcomes and selected
qualification are separate caller-reported attachments.

* Capture
The selected tests must live in an immutable source object. A separate
:test-source can hold tests plus fixtures when the application's build snapshot
contains only its compilation inputs. :cwd is relative to that test source and
is validated without following symlinks. The SDK/product descriptors and every
selected file are hashed; file bytes and secret-bearing output are not copied
into the capsule. Defaults apply only to omitted options: explicit false or
null for cwd/test-source/inputs/tools refuses instead of silently selecting a
default.

#+begin_src clojure
(ns example.test-capsule (:require [artifact.replay :as replay]))

(def capsule
  (replay/capture!
    {:sdk selected-sdk
     :product application-product
     :source application-source
     :test-source immutable-test-source
     :cwd "."
     :tests ["test/example_test.bl"]
     :inputs ["test/fixtures/example.json"]
     :runtime {:compiler compiler-key
               :build build-key
               :loadedNative loaded-native-build-id}
     :tools [{:name "z3" :path canonical-z3-file :sha256 z3-sha256}]}))
#+end_src

The three runtime identities are SHA256 values supplied by the caller's actual
runtime observation. Required tool metadata is a name, canonical regular-file
Nix-store path and SHA256. Resolve tool symlinks before supplying it: the capsule
reader refuses symlinks in a file's path components, including links to other
store objects. This avoids following a stored address outside its declared root.
Tools are streamed and hashed during capture and planning, and must be executable.

Argv is derived from the sorted test selection: test followed by the absolute
immutable test filenames. It cannot name a shell, arbitrary executable, extra
flags or an environment map. Tests are explicit .bl/.bl.md/.bl.org files or
*_test.exs files; directory expansion and fine-grained selector replay are not
implemented. Module loading and test admission remain with the real runner.

* Existing reproduction descriptors
Optional :reproduction accepts the descriptor returned by artifact/capsule! (or
its wrapper containing :descriptor). Only its fixed output/source/derivation,
compiler and loaded-native identities are projected into replay data. Raw
requests, manifests, arbitrary qualification fields and environments are omitted.
Wrapper and descriptor schemas reject unknown or duplicate normalized keys.
Request/manifest source fields reject mixed keyword/string duplicates and
disagreement; their other contents are not serialized.
The projected output/source and compiler/native identities must agree with the
replay declaration. The existing not-recorded qualification marker is retained;
it is never promoted into a passing replay qualification.

* Plan and observations

#+begin_src clojure
(def normalized (replay/validate capsule))
(def plan
  (replay/plan! normalized
    {:sdk actual-sdk
     :runtime {:compiler actual-compiler-key
               :build actual-build-key
               :loadedNative actual-loaded-native-build-id}
     :tools actual-observed-tools}))
#+end_src

validate is pure closed-schema normalization of already decoded records. It
rejects keyword/string aliases of the same field. A JSON ingress must separately
reject duplicate raw object keys before a decoder can discard them.
plan! rechecks selected file bytes,
executable bits, SDK/product descriptor hashes, cwd/root structure and required
tool files. It requires the declared SDK/runtime/tool observations; missing or
changed values refuse rather than imply a match. The supplied observations must
come from the main thread's real runtime/tool inspection. Equality with caller
supplied observations is not itself proof of live runtime identity.

The result has kind=test-admission-plan, status=admission-required and
authority=none. It supplies exact SDK/product/source/test-source identities,
absolute cwd and derived test argv, plus the declared metadata and attached
reports. Main must obtain the existing live execution admission; neither the
plan nor its binding digest substitutes for it. This module does not publish
or retain roots: main/coordinator must durably retain all four identity closures
and declared tool closures before advertising a replay capsule as usable.

* Outcome and qualification attachments
Attachments bind to the exact input binding and contain only fixed labels,
numeric counts and hashes. No stdout, exception text, environment or arbitrary
nested receipt is embedded.

#+begin_src clojure
(def recorded
  (replay/attach-outcome capsule
    {:binding (get capsule "binding") :status "passed"
     :tests 3 :pass 12 :fail 0 :error 0 :exit 0
     :receiptDigest outcome-receipt-sha256}))

(replay/attach-qualification recorded
  {:binding (get capsule "binding") :status "passed"
   :scope "selected-tests-only" :receiptDigest qualification-receipt-sha256})
#+end_src

A passing outcome requires a nonempty test run, zero failures/errors and exit 0.
Passing selected-test qualification requires the matching passing outcome.
These attachments report observations supplied by the caller; schema validation
cannot establish that tests were executed. They never certify a full SDK,
all historical semantic cases, platform compatibility or code activation.

* Bounds and refusal
At most 1024 test/support files are accepted, each at most 16 MiB and 64 MiB in
total. SDK/product artifact.json files are independently bounded to 16 MiB each.
At most 64 tools are accepted, each at most 256 MiB and 1 GiB in total. Hashing uses
64 KiB reads and checks growth against the same budget. EOF size must also
match the initial regular-file size, so truncation does not become a successful
capture. The immutable-store assumption remains necessary; this is not a
general-purpose race-safe reader for attacker-writable filesystem trees. Paths are bounded to 4096
bytes; digests are exactly 64 hexadecimal characters. Duplicate files/tools,
unknown fields, empty selections, traversal, non-regular files, symlink path
components, mutated bindings, inconsistent attachments and missing identities
refuse. File order and equivalent keyword/string-key records normalize to the
same binding; map enumeration order does not determine that digest.

* Validation cases
Exercise the reader, JSON renderer and these boundaries:

- Real immutable SDK/product/test snapshots; equivalent reordered selections and
  keyword/string-key maps produce identical bindings and admission plans.
- Changed/missing test bytes, supporting files, executable bits and descriptor
  bytes; changed or missing observed compiler/build/native/tool identities.
- Absolute/traversing/empty paths, symlink files and intermediate directories,
  empty/duplicate test selections and unsupported test suffixes.
- Forged argv (shell/extra flags), environment fields, opaque resource values,
  unknown keys, excessive file/tool counts and per-file/total byte budgets.
- Native reproduction descriptor projection with matching output/source/runtime,
  plus mismatches and arbitrary nested fields that must never be serialized.
- Explicit false/null optional values, mixed keyword/string duplicate fields,
  duplicate descriptor wrappers and disagreement between request/manifest source.
- Wrong-binding outcome/qualification attachments, null attachment requests, contradictory passing/failing
  counts and passing qualification without a passing nonempty outcome.
- Confirm capture/plan never execute a test or tool, acquire execution grants,
  activate a product, create roots or read a file referenced by outcome metadata.
